brief: Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator (RAI) fell to -0.5, lowest since the April 2025 tariff crash, because the RAI's correlation to Nasdaq 100 performance versus equal-weight S&P 500 has climbed near 1: cross-asset risk appetite is now mostly an AI-trade proxy. Credit did the damage (Goldman's credit risk-appetite gauge near -3, worse than April 2025) while bonds rallied and equities only slipped just below zero, so credit is pricing a tariff-crash-sized scare against equities' mild wobble. Semiconductor sensitivity explains 54% of three-week cross-asset moves versus oil's 2%, and the dollar is trading pro-cyclically. This week's options price Nasdaq/hyperscaler earnings and the Fed/BoJ/ECB decisions as the bigger risk; next week prices US midterms. Goldman expects a Fed hold Wednesday then a December hike, with no central-bank put in sight. Despite that, Goldman stays modestly pro-risk (overweight equities, underweight credit, S&P targets of 8,000/8,700) on earnings support, lighter positioning and cheaper valuations, even as US HY spreads (337bp) already breach its own bear case. Monday's Anthropic S-1 and Meta's $35bn raise sparked a relief rally Goldman's own floor rated an unconvincing 4/10. The RAI is not yet negative enough (below -1, near -2) to trigger Goldman's contrarian buy signal.
